newsitem.title: JAPAN: Decline in Japan surplus slowing -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Decline in Japan surplus slowing -- MOF.

text.p: The decline in Japan's surplus in trade and services is slowing but the surplus is unlikely to rise significantly in the long term, an official of the Ministry of Finance told reporters on Wednesday.
"The decline in the surplus in trade and services is slowing but it (the surplus) is unlikely to rise significantly in the medium-to-longer term," the official said.
He added that Japan continued to post a deficit in its services account but said that the pace of the rise in imports had slowed recently.

The Finance Ministry announced earlier that the surplus in Japan's current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose 92.7 percent to 1.09 trillion yen in April from the previous year.

The MOF official said that the April figures were calculated based on an exchange rate of 125.51 yen to the dollar. This yen rate was 14.4 percent weaker than that used for the previous year's calculation, he said.
